title: Recreational screen use and internalizing problems from preadolescence to young adulthood in a longitudinal twin cohort with co-twin comparison
title_zh: 同卵双胞胎纵向研究：从学龄前到青年期的娱乐屏幕使用与内化问题的关系
abstract: Abstract The mental health impact of increasing recreational screen use among youth has raised substantial concerns, yet questions about causality remain unresolved. Here, leveraging a co-twin control design, we examined associations between screen use and internalizing problems from childhood to early adulthood among 21,797 Swedish twins, accounting for shared familial factors. Recreational screen use was associated with increased internalizing symptoms and clinical diagnosed depression and anxiety. However, these associations were substantially attenuated within discordant twin pairs and did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. These findings suggest that shared genetic and environmental factors partly explain the association between youth screen use and mental health. Although co-twin estimates provided limited evidence for clear causal effects, the association between heavy interactive screen use and clinical risk highlights the need to understand potential mechanisms linking digital behaviours and youth mental health.
abstract_zh: 摘要：青少年娱乐屏幕使用的增加对心理健康的影响引发了广泛关注，但因果关系仍未解决。本文利用同卵双胞胎对照设计，研究了21,797名瑞典双胞胎从童年到早期成年期的屏幕使用与内化问题之间的关联，并控制了共享的家庭因素。结果显示，娱乐屏幕使用与内化症状、临床诊断的抑郁和焦虑呈正相关。然而，在不一致的双胞胎对中，这些关联显著减弱，且在多重检验校正后不再具有统计学显著性。这表明共享的遗传和环境因素在一定程度上解释了青少年屏幕使用与心理健康之间的关联。尽管同卵双胞胎估计对明确的因果效应提供的证据有限，但重度交互式屏幕使用与临床风险之间的关联强调了理解数字行为与青少年心理健康之间潜在机制的必要性。
